title: OMB M-22-09: the goals of the federal zero trust strategy for each pillar, in our own words

controls.title: Identity
controls.statement: Staff use identities managed by the enterprise to reach the applications of their work, and phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication protects them from sophisticated online attacks; agencies manage identity centrally, apply strong multi-factor authentication throughout and take at least one device-level signal into account when they authorize a user.

controls.title: Devices
controls.statement: The agency has a complete inventory of every device it operates and authorizes for government use and can prevent, detect and respond to incidents on them; its assets are inventoried through the continuous diagnostics and mitigation program and its endpoint detection and response tools meet its requirements.

controls.title: Networks
controls.statement: All DNS requests and HTTP traffic in the environment are encrypted, and the agency has begun to plan how to break its perimeter into isolated environments.

controls.title: Applications and workloads
controls.statement: Every application is treated as connected to the internet, is tested rigorously and is open to external reports of vulnerabilities.

controls.title: Data
controls.statement: The agency follows a path to protections that rest on thorough categorization of its data, uses cloud security services that monitor access to sensitive data and logs and shares information across the enterprise.

publisher: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President
